<!-- GENERATED by `bun run generate:docs`. Edit the runtime metadata sources imported by scripts/generate/generate-docs.ts instead. -->

Configure Hunk with TOML settings in your user config or a project's `.hunk/config.toml`. Include only the settings you want to change.

For a walkthrough, start with the [configuration guide](/docs/configure/configuration/). This page lists every supported preference, table, and default.

## Config file locations

| File                | Location                                                                                               | Use for                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| User (XDG override) | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hunk/config.toml`                                                                    | Personal preferences      |
| User (fallback)     | `$HOME/.config/hunk/config.toml`, or `%USERPROFILE%/.config/hunk/config.toml` when HOME is unavailable | Personal preferences      |
| Repository/project  | `.hunk/config.toml` at the project root                                                                | Project-specific settings |

Hunk searches upward from the working directory for the nearest directory containing `.hunk` or recognized by a loaded VCS backend as a repository root. That directory supplies the project config. No user config is loaded if none of the user-path environment variables is set.

Create your user config with a few settings:

```toml
theme = "terminal"
mode = "auto"
line_numbers = true
wrap_lines = false
```

Omitted settings use the built-in defaults below. Shared settings belong **above all table headers**: in TOML, keys after `[show]` belong to that table until another table begins.

## Command tables

### Override settings for a command

Add a command table to the same config file and repeat the settings you want to override. Other settings are inherited. This changes command preferences, not command implementations or keyboard shortcuts.

```toml
mode = "auto"

[vcs]
mode = "split"
watch = true

[show]
mode = "unified"

[diff]
wrap_lines = true
```

With this config and no repository overrides:

| Invocation                             | Result                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `hunk diff`                            | Split layout, watch enabled          |
| `hunk show`                            | Unified layout                       |
| `hunk diff --files before.ts after.ts` | Automatic layout, wrapping enabled   |
| `hunk show --mode split`               | Split layout; the explicit flag wins |

**Repository `hunk diff` uses `[vcs]`. `[diff]` only applies to two-file comparisons.** Table names are fixed; do not infer additional tables from CLI command names.

| Table          | Applies to                                                |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[open]`       | complete documents and directory browsing (`hunk open`)   |
| `[vcs]`        | working-tree and target reviews (`hunk diff`)             |
| `[show]`       | commit and target display reviews (`hunk show`)           |
| `[stash-show]` | stash reviews (`hunk stash show`)                         |
| `[diff]`       | two-file comparisons (`hunk diff --files <left> <right>`) |
| `[patch]`      | patch-file reviews (`hunk patch`)                         |
| `[difftool]`   | Git difftool pair reviews (`hunk difftool`)               |

### Pager settings

`[pager]` applies when a diff opens as a pager session: Git output displayed by `hunk pager`, or any review launched with `--pager`. It overrides the matching command table **within the same file**, not in ordinary interactive reviews. `hunk pager` reviews match `[patch]`.

```toml
[pager]
mode = "unified"
wrap_lines = true
```

Try it for one Git invocation:

```bash
git -c core.pager="hunk pager" diff
```

Pager reviews start with the files pane closed, even if `sidebar = true`, and hide the menu bar unless a config layer sets `menu_bar`. Non-diff input goes to a plain-text pager instead; these view preferences do not configure that fallback. See [Git pager and difftool](/docs/workflows/git-pager-and-difftool/) for permanent setup.

## Resolution and scope

Layers apply from lowest to highest precedence:

1. built-in defaults
2. user config top-level keys, then the matching command table, then `[pager]` when pager chrome is active
3. repository `.hunk/config.toml` top-level keys, matching command table, and pager table
4. explicit CLI options

A repository's top-level setting can override a user command-specific setting. For example:

```toml
# User config
[show]
mode = "unified"
```

```toml
# Repository .hunk/config.toml
mode = "split"
```

`hunk show` uses split; `hunk show --mode unified` uses unified. Flags such as `--no-wrap` also override a configured `wrap_lines = true`. See the [CLI reference](/docs/reference/cli/) for available flags.

Preference keys may appear at top level, in a command table, or in `[pager]`, except that user-only preferences are ignored in repository config. Theme definitions, extension tables, and keybindings belong at the root, never nested in command tables.

Persistent application state uses an absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME/hunk/state.json`, falling back to `~/.local/state/hunk/state.json` (or the platform home equivalent). On first use, Hunk copies legacy state from the config directory only when the new file is absent, retains the original, and continues using it if migration fails. Existing new state always takes precedence. Global extensions remain in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hunk/extensions/` or `~/.config/hunk/extensions/`.

## Preference keys

### Layout and display

#### `mode`

Choose diff layout. `auto` uses split on wide terminals and unified on narrow ones; `split` and `unified` force that layout.

- **Type:** string
- **Accepted:** `auto`, `split`, `unified`, or deprecated alias `stack`
- **Built-in default:** `auto`

#### `auto_split_min_width`

Minimum available diff width, in columns, for split diffs in `auto` mode, after side panes and outer padding; narrower diff areas show unified diffs.

- **Type:** integer
- **Accepted:** a positive number of terminal columns
- **Built-in default:** `160`

#### `theme`

Select the color theme. `terminal` follows the terminal palette; `auto` chooses a light or dark GitHub theme from the terminal background (dark fallback).

- **Type:** string
- **Accepted:** `terminal`, `auto`, a built-in theme id, or a custom theme id
- **Built-in default:** `github-dark-default`

#### `line_numbers`

Show old and new line-number columns.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `true`

#### `tab_width`

Set terminal-cell tab stops used for display and wrapping.

- **Type:** integer
- **Accepted:** 1 through 16
- **Built-in default:** `4`

#### `file_gap`

Rows between files in the review stream, including the `─` rule. `1` keeps the current rule; `0` hides it; larger values add blank rows above it.

- **Type:** integer
- **Accepted:** 0 through 8
- **Built-in default:** `1`

#### `hunk_gap`

Blank rows before each hunk after the first in a file.

- **Type:** integer
- **Accepted:** 0 through 8
- **Built-in default:** `0`

#### `wrap_lines`

Wrap long diff lines instead of keeping one visual row.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `false`

#### `hunk_headers`

Show hunk metadata rows in the review stream.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `true`

#### `menu_bar`

Show the top application menu bar.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `true`

#### `animations`

Animate panes as they open and close.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `true`

#### `sidebar`

Show the files pane if it fits, keep it closed, or let the responsive layout decide. Pager sessions always open with the files pane closed.

- **Type:** string or boolean
- **Accepted:** `"auto"`, `true`, or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `auto`

#### `transparent_background`

Let the terminal background show through Hunk surfaces.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `false`
- **Aliases:** `transparentBackground` (deprecated)

#### `color_moved`

Request moved-line coloring for Git reviews. `true` requests zebra coloring when Git has no diff.colorMoved setting; an explicit Git setting takes precedence, even when this preference is false.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** not set; Git uses its diff.colorMoved setting

### Navigation and scrolling

#### `cursor_line`

Mark the current line as a full-row highlight or on its line number. `off` restores plain `j`/`k` scrolling.

- **Type:** string
- **Accepted:** `row`, `number`, or `off`
- **Built-in default:** `row`

#### `scroll_off`

Keep the current line at least this many rows clear of the viewport top/bottom edge while stepping through a diff, like Vim's `scrolloff`.

- **Type:** integer
- **Accepted:** 0 through 40
- **Built-in default:** `5`

#### `wheel_scroll_lines`

Set review rows per vertical wheel event. `auto` keeps cadence-based acceleration from one to three rows.

- **Type:** string or integer
- **Accepted:** `auto` or 1 through 10
- **Built-in default:** `auto`
- **Scope:** user config only

### Review inputs and reloading

#### `vcs`

Select the version-control adapter explicitly. An explicit id outranks detection; an id no loaded backend owns falls back to detection with a startup notice.

- **Type:** string
- **Accepted:** `git`, `jj`, `sl`, or an id a loaded extension backend registers
- **Built-in default:** detected from the checkout (Git fallback)

#### `watch`

Reload supported review inputs when their source changes.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `false`

#### `exclude_untracked`

Hide untracked files from working-tree reviews.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `false`

### Notes and copying

#### `agent_notes`

Show agent notes when a review opens.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `false`

#### `copy_decorations`

Include diff signs and line numbers in copied selections.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `false`

### Saving preferences

#### `prompt_save_view_preferences`

Ask before discarding view changes that can be persisted.

- **Type:** boolean
- **Accepted:** `true` or `false`
- **Built-in default:** `true`

## Keyboard shortcuts

To change the keys that trigger actions, use `[keybindings]` in your **user config**:

```toml
[keybindings]
"hunk.review.nextHunk" = ["]", "ctrl+n"]
"hunk.app.quit" = "ctrl+x"
```

Your bindings replace that command's default keys. Repository config cannot remap keys. See [Keybindings](/docs/configure/keybindings/) for command ids, unbinding, conflicts, and chord syntax.

## Custom themes

Choose a built-in theme with `theme = "catppuccin-mocha"`. `terminal` follows your terminal palette; `auto` selects a light or dark GitHub theme from the terminal background. See the [theme guide](/docs/configure/themes/) for selection and previews.

To customize colors:

```toml
theme = "custom"

[custom_theme]
base = "catppuccin-mocha"
accent = "#7fd1ff"
```

The theme inherits its base and overrides only the colors you supply.

### Named themes

Use root `[themes.<id>]` tables to keep several custom themes:

```toml
theme = "midnight-ink"

[themes.midnight-ink]
base = "catppuccin-mocha"
accent = "#7fd1ff"

[themes.paper-trail]
base = "github-light-default"
```

Each accepts the same keys as `[custom_theme]`. Select one with `theme = "<id>"` or `--theme <id>`; `[custom_theme]` itself has the id `custom`. Ids use lowercase letters or digits separated by `-` or `_`. Reserved ids (built-in themes, `auto`, and `custom`) are skipped with a startup notice. Same-id theme tables merge field by field across user and repository config, with repository values winning.

### Semantic colors

`custom_theme.label` accepts a non-empty display name. Every semantic color below accepts a six-digit `#rrggbb` value:

| Key                                | Description                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `custom_theme.background`          | Main application background.                                        |
| `custom_theme.panel`               | Pane and menu backgrounds.                                          |
| `custom_theme.panelAlt`            | Alternate backgrounds, including diff metadata and the status line. |
| `custom_theme.border`              | Pane separators and borders.                                        |
| `custom_theme.accent`              | Active controls and highlighted UI elements.                        |
| `custom_theme.accentMuted`         | Tinted backgrounds for selected controls and tree entries.          |
| `custom_theme.text`                | Default foreground text.                                            |
| `custom_theme.muted`               | Secondary labels and metadata text.                                 |
| `custom_theme.addedBg`             | Added-line background.                                              |
| `custom_theme.removedBg`           | Removed-line background.                                            |
| `custom_theme.movedAddedBg`        | Background for the added side of moved lines.                       |
| `custom_theme.movedRemovedBg`      | Background for the removed side of moved lines.                     |
| `custom_theme.contextBg`           | Unchanged-line background.                                          |
| `custom_theme.addedContentBg`      | Emphasized changed text within added lines.                         |
| `custom_theme.removedContentBg`    | Emphasized changed text within removed lines.                       |
| `custom_theme.contextContentBg`    | Content background within unchanged lines.                          |
| `custom_theme.addedSignColor`      | Addition markers in the diff gutter.                                |
| `custom_theme.removedSignColor`    | Deletion markers in the diff gutter.                                |
| `custom_theme.lineNumberBg`        | Line-number column background.                                      |
| `custom_theme.lineNumberFg`        | Line-number text.                                                   |
| `custom_theme.selectedHunk`        | Selected-hunk highlighting.                                         |
| `custom_theme.badgeAdded`          | Addition-count badges.                                              |
| `custom_theme.badgeRemoved`        | Deletion-count badges.                                              |
| `custom_theme.badgeNeutral`        | Neutral badges and file-header labels.                              |
| `custom_theme.fileNew`             | New-file status indicators.                                         |
| `custom_theme.fileDeleted`         | Deleted-file status indicators.                                     |
| `custom_theme.fileRenamed`         | Renamed-file status indicators.                                     |
| `custom_theme.fileModified`        | Modified-file status indicators.                                    |
| `custom_theme.fileUntracked`       | Untracked-file status indicators.                                   |
| `custom_theme.noteBorder`          | Note-card borders and inline note guides.                           |
| `custom_theme.noteBackground`      | Note-card body background.                                          |
| `custom_theme.noteTitleBackground` | Note-card title background.                                         |
| `custom_theme.noteTitleText`       | Note-card title text.                                               |

### Syntax scopes

`[custom_theme.syntax_scopes]` accepts non-empty Shiki/TextMate scope names and six-digit hex colors. Add overrides to your custom theme; quote keys containing dots:

```toml
[custom_theme.syntax_scopes]
"comment" = "#6e85a7"
"punctuation.definition.comment" = "#6e85a7"
```

These are syntax token colors, distinct from the UI and diff backgrounds above. See the [theme guide](/docs/configure/themes/#create-a-custom-theme) for scope matching behavior.

The deprecated `[custom_theme.syntax]` table remains accepted for one compatibility window with these semantic keys: `custom_theme.syntax.default`, `custom_theme.syntax.keyword`, `custom_theme.syntax.string`, `custom_theme.syntax.comment`, `custom_theme.syntax.number`, `custom_theme.syntax.function`, `custom_theme.syntax.property`, `custom_theme.syntax.type`, `custom_theme.syntax.variable`, `custom_theme.syntax.operator`, `custom_theme.syntax.punctuation`. Hunk normalizes them into exact scope overrides and emits a startup notice.

## Extensions

`[extensions]` controls extension loading. It is root-only and does not accept command or `[pager]` overrides. For example, disable the bundled GitHub integration:

```toml
[extensions]
disabled = ["hunk.gh"]
```

`enabled = false` and `--no-extensions` turn off user extensions; bundled VCS backends still load. Selectable bundled extensions such as `hunk.gh` can be disabled by id.

| Key                   | Type             | Accepted                      | Built-in default | Description                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extensions.enabled`  | boolean          | `true` or `false`             | `true`           | Load user extensions. `--no-extensions` forces this off for one run, and bundled VCS backends stay loaded either way.                  |
| `extensions.paths`    | array of strings | entry file or directory paths | `[]`             | Extension entry points loaded at startup. Paths a repository config contributes are trust-gated before they run.                       |
| `extensions.disabled` | array of strings | exact extension identities    | `[]`             | Disable selectable bundled or user extensions before their factories or modules execute. User and repository lists combine as a union. |

Repository `.hunk/config.toml` paths are kept separate from user paths: Hunk prompts for trust before executing repository-declared extension code, and `--no-extensions` disables user extensions entirely for one run.

Each extension reads its own settings from a root `[extension.<id>]` table. For example, after installing the [collapse-generated example extension](/docs/extend/extensions/#a-complete-example):

```toml
[extension.collapse-generated]
patterns = ["*.lock", "generated/*"]
```

These keys belong to that extension, not Hunk's preference catalog. Repository tables merge over user tables key by key, and Hunk reports which extension settings the repository overrides. See [Extensions](/docs/extend/extensions/) for installation, trust, loading controls, and examples.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem                                   | Check                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `[diff]` does not affect `hunk diff`      | Use `[vcs]` for repository reviews.                                           |
| A preference seems ignored                | Check repository config, then explicit CLI flags. Later layers win.           |
| A shared setting affects only one command | Move it above all table headers.                                              |
| A shortcut remap has no effect            | Put `[keybindings]` in user config; check command ids and reported conflicts. |
| Custom colors have no effect              | Select the custom theme by id and keep its definition at the root.            |
